messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — KV cache growth and continuous-batching latency spike detected for route /v1/generate (us-west). Alert: kv-cache-high-mem + cbatch-latency-95. Affected: dedicated customers on pool gw-usw-03. Symptoms: KV cache size skyrocketing, batching queue depth increase, 95th latency ~3x baseline, some 503s. Please acknowledge and follow runbook: https://internal/runbooks/kvcache-cbatch
Oncall: ack — I'm on it, investigating hot paths and recent deploys. Pulling perf graphs and recent KVS ops now.
Alice M: I see a large increase in speculative write volume to kv-store around 2112345600. Drafts written to KV far more often than targets; looks like speculative decoding is creating extra prefixes and not reconciling them. Might explain cache blowup.
Ben T: Confirmed. Top keys are prefixed by "spec:draft:" and we see lots of short-lived prefixes that bypass our LRU heuristics. Also continuous-batch window size spiked for many requests (longer wait -> bigger batches).
Carla R: Immediate mitigations proposal: 1) Temporarily disable speculative decoding for route /v1/generate (will reduce KV churn). 2) Cap continuous-batch settings on gw-usw-03: max_batch_ms=100, max_batch_tokens=64. 3) Run targeted KV flush of speculative prefixes for pool gw-usw-03.
Oncall: I can patch routing flag now. Rolling to canary (10% traffic) first. Will also push batch config change to canary.
Ben T: +1. We should avoid a full cluster flush; flush only keys with prefix "spec:draft:gw-usw-03". Command below.
Carla R: Paste of commands:
```bash
# disable speculative decoding for route
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","speculative_decoding":false}'

# apply batch caps to pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/pools/gw-usw-03/config -d '{"max_batch_ms":100,"max_batch_tokens":64}'

# targeted kv flush (speculative prefixes)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://kvs.internal/pools/gw-usw-03/admin/flush -d '{"prefix":"spec:draft:gw-usw-03"}'
```
Oncall: Pushing flag to canary now. Rolling patch id: deploy-211234-flag1. Canary for route at 10% traffic. Watching metrics.
incident-bot: UPDATE — canary deployed (deploy-211234-flag1). Observability: queue depth down ~20% at canary nodes within 90s.
Eva S: Customer impact quick note: two dedicated customers (acct-844 and acct-921) reporting slow responses and transient errors. 95th latency for those tenants went from ~120ms -> ~1.1-1.4s at peak. ~14 503s observed in last 12m. No data loss.
Frank L: Logs show KV write error rate decreased after canary. Also seeing fewer long polls. Good signal.
Oncall: Based on canary success, rolling the flag and batch caps to 50% (deploy-211234-flag2). Will delay full 100% for 5m observation.
Carla R: After we stabilize, we still need a hotfix to prevent speculative writes from generating unique per-draft prefixes for every minor token mismatch. Likely bug in speculative-to-target reconciliation when draft length < target length under continuous batching.
Ben T: Noted. Quick patch idea: change KV write keying to include a stable draft hash instead of full draft text, and add TTL=30s for speculative keys. That reduces LRU pressure. Will sketch patch in next 90m.
incident-bot: STATUS — mitigation in progress. Route flag disabled on 50% of traffic; batch caps applied to gw-usw-03 on 50% of nodes. Total KV pool memory for gw-usw-03 trending down.
Oncall: Rolling to 100% now (deploy-211234-flag3). Monitoring final 10m.
incident-bot: RESOLVED (mitigated) — Route level speculative decoding disabled + batch caps applied cluster-wide. KV speculative prefix flush completed for gw-usw-03. High memory and 95th latency spike subsided to within acceptable bounds.
Eva S: Summary for customers: We mitigated an internal KV cache churn caused by speculative decoding + long batching windows. Tail latency returned to baseline. Impact: degraded latency and ~20 503s across two dedicated customers for ~20m window (start 2112345600 - mitigated by 2112345775).
Oncall: Handoff to next oncall @Frank L for post-incident cleanup and RCA. Key followups for next 24h: 
- Complete hotfix to change speculative keying and TTL (owner: Ben T)
- Add guard in batching layer to avoid unbounded queue growth when speculative write rate > threshold (owner: Carla R)
- Add metric: speculative_kv_write_rate and an oncall alert threshold (owner: Alice M)
- Customer comms draft for impacted tenants (owner: Eva S)

Frank L: Acked, taking handoff. I'll keep the incident thread open and update when hotfix lands.
Carla R: Also adding postmortem doc and will include timeline + dashboard links. Link to live graphs: https://observability.internal/dashboards/kvcache-cbatch-211234
Oncall: Thanks all — great quick coordination. Closing pager. Transitioning to postmortem state. :thumbsup:
